item.title: Markov-Switching Model Cuts Sensor Network Latency by 44.9% - Bioengineer.org
item.description:
요약

  • Subject of Research: A constrained-state Markov-switching new media spatial sensor network
  • Article Title: A constrained-state Markov-switching new media spatial sensor network
  • A constrained-state Markov-switching new media spatial sensor network. Discover Computing, 29(1), Article 770. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10791-026-10666-0

본문

Researchers at the intersection of digital media technology and the Internet of Things have proposed a constrained-state Markov-switching new media spatial sensor network, or CSMJ-NMSN, designed to resolve the critical decoupling between information fusion and network transmission control. Published in Discover Computing in October 2026, the study addresses the specific bottleneck of mode observation uncertainty in complex urban open environments. By integrating a hidden Markov jump system with hard physical constraints on energy and cache, the architecture aims to ensure low-latency transmission of multimedia data while preventing the premature failure of resource-constrained sensing nodes.

The core challenge in new media spatial sensing networks is that existing fusion methods often prioritize accuracy without adapting to real-time network states, while control strategies are typically designed independently of the fusion process. This separation can lead to congestion collapse or node death under bursty traffic loads. The proposed architecture introduces a synergistic fusion-prediction-control closed-loop system that dynamically co-optimizes data compression, mode perception, and transmission parameters. This approach ensures that data generation is inherently network-aware, allowing the system to anticipate congestion trends and adjust transmission behavior proactively rather than reactively.

The methodology is built upon a hierarchical distributed network architecture divided into three layers: the physical perception layer, the information fusion layer, and the constraint control layer. The physical layer consists of heterogeneous sensor nodes, including environmental sensors and new media devices such as cameras and microphones, deployed in a distributed manner. These nodes collect multi-modal raw data and forward it to the fusion layer, which utilizes strong tracking filtering and two-dimensional entropy to extract low-dimensional, high-fidelity state features. This process minimizes the volume of transmitted data while preserving the accuracy required for reliable control decisions.

At the constraint control layer, the network evolution is modeled as a discrete-time hidden Markov jump system with four distinct modes: normal, energy warning, congestion, and topology reconstruction. Due to the unreliability of wireless communication, the aggregation node’s observation of the current network mode often suffers from delays and packet losses. To overcome this, the system employs a hidden Markov observation model and the forward algorithm to estimate the true network mode in real time. This forward-looking mode perception allows the controller to anticipate energy warnings and congestion trends, enabling the adoption of energy-saving measures before constraint violations occur.

item.title: INVE 테크놀로지스, IoT 사업 매각 이익 산출 내역 공개…인수에 3000만 달러 배정 - 데이터투자
item.description:
요약

  • 3분기 분기보고서 제출…현금 2341만 달러 지급하고 트랙소노미 우선주 5000만 달러어치 받아
  • 보고서에 따르면 회사는 태국 자회사 아이덴티브 타일랜드(Identiv (Thailand) Co., Ltd) 지분을 포함한 IoT 사업 영업자산 대부분과 함께 조정 대상인 현금 2500만 달러를 트랙소노미 시스템즈(Trackonomy Systems, Inc.)에 넘겼다.
  • 그 대가로 트랙소노미의 시리즈 C 우선주 5000만 달러어치(주당 공정가치 20.07달러)를 받았고, 트랙소노미는 IoT 사업 관련 일부 부채를 인수했다.

본문

3분기 분기보고서 제출…현금 2341만 달러 지급하고 트랙소노미 우선주 5000만 달러어치 받아

보고서에 따르면 회사는 태국 자회사 아이덴티브 타일랜드(Identiv (Thailand) Co., Ltd) 지분을 포함한 IoT 사업 영업자산 대부분과 함께 조정 대상인 현금 2500만 달러를 트랙소노미 시스템즈(Trackonomy Systems, Inc.)에 넘겼다. 그 대가로 트랙소노미의 시리즈 C 우선주 5000만 달러어치(주당 공정가치 20.07달러)를 받았고, 트랙소노미는 IoT 사업 관련 일부 부채를 인수했다. 이 거래는 9월 10일 연례 주주총회에서 승인됐으며, 회사는 9월 30일 현재 이 우선주 249만 1281주를 보유하고 있다.

매각 이익 612만 7000달러는 매각 대가 5000만 달러에서 매각 관련 현금 지급액 2341만 1000달러, 매각한 순자산 1750만 8000달러, 순운전자본 등 사후 정산 조정액 246만 5000달러, 거래 관련 비용 48만 9000달러를 뺀 값이다. 매각 시점 IoT 사업의 자산은 2032만 달러, 부채는 281만 2000달러였다. 회사는 사후 정산 조정분 250만 달러를 미지급금으로 계상해 매각 이익에서 차감했고, 이 금액은 4분기에 지급했다.

트랙소노미 우선주는 공정가치를 쉽게 알 수 없는 비상장 지분이어서 원가에서 손상을 빼고 같은 발행사의 동일·유사 증권에서 관찰되는 가격 변동을 반영하는 측정 대안 방식으로 회계 처리한다. 회사는 보고 기간 중 손상 징후는 없었다고 밝혔다. 회사는 매각 종결과 함께 6~12개월 동안 트랙소노미에 정보기술(IT)·인력을 지원하는 전환 서비스 계약도 맺었으며, 3분기 이 계약에서 발생한 수수료는 미미했다.

에드워드 커른바우어(Edward Kirnbauer) 최고재무책임자(CFO) 등 일부 직원은 자산 매각과 관련한 거래 보너스를 받을 자격이 있다. 보너스는 매각 종결 후 6~12개월의 잔류 기간이 끝나는 시점과 회사 해산 시점 중 이른 때에 지급되며, 원칙적으로 그때까지 계속 근무해야 한다. 회사는 지난 9월 전임 최고경영자(CEO)가 사임하고 임시 CEO가 선임됐다며, 정식 CEO 등 경영진 확보가 향후 실적을 좌우할 것이라고 밝혔다.

인수 3000만 달러 배정과 운영비 계획

회사는 매각 이후 상업적 영업 매출이 없는 상태에서 규제 산업의 기업용 서비스형 소프트웨어(SaaS) 기업 인수를 추진하고 있다. 대상 시장으로는 의료 운영, 작업자 안전(EHS), 의약품 공급망, 식품 안전, 의료기기 규제 준수, 환경·수질 관리, 산업 운영을 꼽았다. 회사는 가능한 한 빨리 인수를 마무리할 계획이지만 예정대로 성사된다는 보장은 없다고 밝혔다.

회사는 인수에 약 3000만 달러를 배정하고, 2027년부터 약 3년에 걸쳐 본사 관리비와 상장사 운영 비용으로 약 1200만~1500만 달러를 쓸 것으로 예상했다. 인수 대금은 현금과 함께 기간 가득형 주식, 프리미엄 가격의 옵션·워런트, 성과 연동 언아웃 등을 섞어 마련할 방침이다. 향후 현금 유입은 트랙소노미 전환 서비스 대금(발생하는 경우)과 이자수익으로 이뤄질 것이라고 회사는 설명했다.

9월 30일 기준 운전자본은 8140만 달러로 지난해 말 1억 3330만 달러보다 5190만 달러 줄었다. 1~9월 영업활동 현금 유출은 1377만 6000달러로 전년 동기 972만 9000달러보다 늘었고, 투자활동 현금 유출은 매각 관련 현금 지급액을 포함해 2517만 5000달러였다. 9월 30일 기준 누적 결손금은 3억 6560만 달러이며, 회사는 보유 현금으로 향후 최소 12개월간 운영 자금을 충당할 수 있다고 판단했다.

회사는 자사주 매입 프로그램에 따라 1~9월 보통주 61만 1144주를 180만 달러에 사들였다. 월별로는 8월 52만 6014주(평균 2.88달러), 9월 8만 5130주(평균 2.81달러)다. 프로그램 시행 이후 누적 매입은 107만 4923주, 약 370만 달러다. 이와 별도로 RSU 가득에 따른 직원 원천징수 세금 납부를 위해 보통주 30만 8335주(92만 9000달러)를 매입했다. 회사는 분기 종료 후인 10월 21일 주당 2.85~3.40달러로 최대 2000만 달러 규모의 수정 더치 옥션 방식 자사주 공개매수에 착수했으며, 이 공개매수는 뉴욕 시간 기준 11월 19일 오후 5시에 마감된다.

회사는 위험 요인에서 IoT 사업 매각 이후 나스닥 상장 규정상 '공개 셸(public shell)' 회사로 간주될 수 있으며, 그 경우 상장폐지 절차나 더 엄격한 상장 요건이 적용될 수 있다고 밝혔다. 현재 나스닥 상장폐지 계획은 없다고 덧붙였다. 1940년 투자회사법(Investment Company Act)상 투자회사로 간주되면 사업 전략 실행이 어려워져 회사를 청산하거나 정리하기로 결정할 수도 있다고 적었다.

트랙소노미 우선주는 공개시장이 없고 양도 제한이 붙어 있어 원하는 시점이나 가격에 처분하지 못할 수 있다고 회사는 밝혔다. 비상장사인 트랙소노미의 재무·영업 정보는 회계 처리상 공시가 필요한 범위 외에는 정기적으로 제공할 계획이 없다고 덧붙였다.

INVE 테크놀로지스는 IoT 사업 매각 후 아이덴티브(Identiv)에서 사명을 바꾼 회사로, 규제 산업에서 피지컬 AI(Physical AI)를 접목할 기업용 SaaS 사업의 인수·운영을 추진하고 있다. 본사는 미국 캘리포니아주 산타애나에 있다.

박노중 데이터투자 기자 netpark@datatooza.com

item.title: Autonomous Governance Framework Combines Agentic AI and Zero Trust Security - Bioengineer.org
item.description:
요약

  • Subject of Research: Autonomous cybersecurity governance integrating agentic artificial intelligence and zero trust architecture
  • Article Title: Autonomous governance integrating agentic AI and zero trust for intelligent cybersecurity in distributed enterprise ecosystems
  • Autonomous governance integrating agentic AI and zero trust for intelligent cybersecurity in distributed enterprise ecosystems. Discover Internet of Things, 6(1), Article 161. https://doi.org/10.1007/s43926-026-00497-2

본문

A comprehensive review published in Discover Internet of Things by researchers Supreet Nagi, Manpinder Singh Panesar, and Svarmit Singh Pasricha presents an Autonomous Governance Framework designed to address the escalating security complexities of distributed enterprise infrastructures. Modern organizations have rapidly migrated from centralized, on-premises networks to highly distributed, cloud-native environments characterized by multi-cloud implementations, microservice architectures, and pervasive application programming interface endpoints. According to the authors, these decentralized configurations have dismantled the traditional enterprise perimeter, rendering conventional static defenses and manual security oversight increasingly ineffective against sophisticated, automated threats. To counter these challenges, the authors synthesized recent developments in cybersecurity to introduce an autonomous framework that unites Zero Trust Architecture with Agentic Artificial Intelligence. This conceptual integration establishes a continuous closed-loop security posture capable of real-time monitoring, predictive threat modeling, and self-governing policy enforcement across interconnected enterprise operations.

The shift toward distributed computing, remote work environments, and decentralized applications has eliminated the assumption that internal network zones are inherently safe while external traffic is hostile. The review highlights that modern enterprise systems increasingly depend on Internet of Things gadgets, containerized microservices, and autonomous computer agents communicating directly with one another. While these technologies substantially enhance organizational flexibility and operational efficiency, they expand attack surfaces and introduce fluid risk vectors. Specifically, unmanaged machine-to-machine interactions and automated data exchanges can facilitate cascading system failures or widespread data exfiltration if an internal component becomes compromised. The authors note that legacy security models relying on pre-established rules, rigid access thresholds, and periodic human reviews cannot match the execution speed of contemporary cyberattacks. Consequently, enterprise protection requires transitioning from static perimeter defenses to dynamic, data-centric systems that continually authenticate every digital request regardless of origin.

item.title: Hybrid Algorithm Improves 6G Massive MIMO Spectral Efficiency in Simulated IoT Networks - Bioengineer.org
item.description:
요약

  • Subject of Research: Optimization of joint hybrid beamforming and underlay spectrum sharing in 6G massive MIMO IoT networks
  • Article Title: Adaptive DEBKA for joint beamforming and spectrum sharing in 6G massive MIMO IoT networks
  • Adaptive DEBKA for joint beamforming and spectrum sharing in 6G massive MIMO IoT networks. Discover Internet of Things, 6(1), Article 166. https://doi.org/10.1007/s43926-026-00509-1

본문

In simulated wireless communications research, an optimization algorithm known as the Differential Evolution-Enhanced Adaptive Black-Winged Kite Algorithm demonstrated substantial performance improvements for joint hybrid beamforming and underlay spectrum sharing across dense sixth-generation Internet-of-Things networks. Conducted by researchers Wenjian Zhang and Ping Li and published in Discover Internet of Things, the numerical study evaluated how coordinated radio-frequency beamforming and dynamic frequency allocation can overcome severe physical-layer bottlenecks in massive multiple-input multiple-output base stations. Under a default simulated configuration comprising 128 transmit antennas, eight radio-frequency chains, 50 single-antenna devices, and 16 shared subchannels, the proposed algorithm attained an aggregate spectral efficiency of 15.87 ± 0.19 bits per second per Hertz over 30 independent Monte Carlo trials. This performance represents an advantage of 27.5 percent over the manifold-optimization alternating minimization baseline and 8.1 percent over the static hybrid BKAPI method. Furthermore, the search procedure achieved its one-percent convergence stopping threshold in an average of 185 ± 12 iterations, substantially reducing the iteration count required by standard metaheuristic benchmarks while enforcing strict hardware and interference boundaries.

The engineering challenge addressed by the study stems from the fundamental architecture of massive multiple-input multiple-output systems envisioned for upcoming 6G applications, including industrial automation, immersive communication, and intelligent transportation infrastructure. To mitigate these hardware burdens, network designers implement hybrid analog and digital beamforming, which cascades a low-dimensional digital baseband precoder with an analog phase-shifting network driven by a drastically smaller pool of radio-frequency chains. While hybrid architectures preserve much of the spatial multiplexing and array gain of fully digital setups, the physical phase shifters impose non-convex constant-modulus constraints where the magnitude of each analog precoding element must remain fixed to a constant unit value while only its phase angle is adjusted. Compounding this challenge, massive Internet-of-Things deployments require multiple devices to concurrently share identical subchannels, demanding meticulous multi-user interference management alongside strict interference-temperature constraints to protect primary licensed incumbents.

item.title: Smart Bin IoT Network Tests Waste Monitoring Across Bukavu Pilot Sites - Bioengineer.org
item.description:
요약

  • Subject of Research: Internet of Things network architecture for urban waste monitoring in Bukavu
  • Article Title: Design of an IoT sensor-based network architecture for waste collection in Bukavu city (DRC)
  • Design of an IoT sensor-based network architecture for waste collection in Bukavu city (DRC).

본문

A twelve-week pilot deployment of an Internet of Things network architecture in the eastern city of Bukavu in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has demonstrated the technical feasibility of real-time bin monitoring and algorithmic route optimization under challenging urban and topographical conditions. Researchers designed and evaluated a multi-tier framework that pairs downward-facing ultrasonic distance sensors installed in waste receptacles with low-power wide-area wireless transmissions and an open-source data analytics engine. In Bukavu, rapid urbanization, steep topography, and degraded secondary road infrastructure have combined to create severe municipal waste management deficits, where approximately 898 tons of solid waste are generated each day but formal municipal collection systems capture only about seven percent, or roughly 62.86 tons daily. Uncollected waste frequently accumulates across informal dumping sites located in drainage gutters, water collection areas, and public spaces, exacerbating environmental contamination and public health risks related to cholera and malaria transmission.

To evaluate whether low-power digital infrastructure could establish reliable monitoring in an environment marked by severe electrical and connectivity limitations, the investigation deployed seven smart waste bin prototypes across residential, dense, and peri-urban neighborhoods. The hardware architecture selected for the field test utilized Milesight EM310-UDL ultrasonic distance sensors, which were chosen following comparative assessments against alternative units such as the DF703 due to their operating range of up to 450 centimeters, wide angular accuracy of 60 degrees, and integrated accelerometer capabilities. The sensors operate on long-life batteries specified for up to ten years of service, an essential attribute given that only 17.8 percent of household energy needs in Bukavu are met by the electrical grid. To transmit data without incurring recurrent cellular subscription charges or exceeding local power constraints, the team configured the sensors to transmit over the LoRaWAN wireless protocol across the 863 to 870 megahertz frequency plan, routing packets through a centrally placed Things Indoor Gateway connected via an intermediate server on The Things Network.

item.title: Reinforcement Learning Prototype Bolsters LoRaWAN Data Delivery and Transmission Efficiency - Bioengineer.org
item.description:
요약

  • Subject of Research: Deep reinforcement learning for adaptive authenticated encryption and dynamic LoRaWAN transmission control
  • Article Title: Deep reinforcement learning-optimized adaptive authenticated encryption and dynamic transmission control for secure LoRaWAN IoT communication
  • Deep reinforcement learning-optimized adaptive authenticated encryption and dynamic transmission control for secure LoRaWAN IoT communication. Discover Internet of Things, 6(1), Article 170. https://doi.org/10.1007/s43926-026-00515-3

본문

In an experimental trial evaluating low-power wide-area networking hardware under laboratory conditions, researchers deployed a reinforcement learning framework that dynamically tuned both cryptographic key creation and wireless radio transmission settings, demonstrating simultaneous improvements in communications reliability, energy efficiency, and security against unauthorized packet replay. Engineering researchers G. Abinaya, P. Sundaravadivel, S. Vasudevan, and K. Muthulakshmi validated the architecture across twenty consecutive real-time transmission cycles over a controlled fifteen-metre indoor line-of-sight path using a single physical sensor node. According to findings published in Discover Internet of Things, the integrated setup achieved a mean data-recovery rate between 93.7 percent and 96.5 percent across the transmission runs, representing the proportion of transmitted environmental sensor readings that were accurately decrypted and verified at the receiver. Relative to conventional static LoRaWAN baselines, the adaptive system demonstrated a 27.8 percent enhancement in packet delivery ratio while reducing energy consumption by 32.5 percent, all while recording a zero percent replay acceptance rate across all tested adversarial replay scenarios.

Conventional implementations of the Long Range protocol stack, widely known as LoRaWAN, have expanded significantly across industrial automation, municipal infrastructure, and environmental monitoring due to their capability to transmit over extensive distances with sub-milliwatt power draw. However, standard deployments operating under the LoRaWAN 1.0.x specification rely on statically provisioned network session keys and application session keys derived from fixed pre-shared root credentials. These static cryptographic keys remain vulnerable to extraction through physical device theft, brute-force key search over extended lifespans, and packet replay attacks facilitated by poorly synchronized or captured frame counters. At the same time, conventional nodes typically maintain fixed radio physical-layer parameters, including spreading factors ranging from seven to twelve, transmission power levels, and forward error correction coding rates. Because physical wireless channels experience dynamic variations such as multipath fading, environmental attenuation, and background radio-frequency interference, fixed parameters frequently yield inefficient power consumption, elevated packet loss, and degraded service quality that existing heuristic adaptive mechanisms fail to resolve quickly.

item.title: Adaptive Federated Learning Framework Boosts Industrial Sensor Fault Detection to 92.6 Percent - Bioengineer.org
item.description:
요약

  • Subject of Research: Adaptive federated learning and sensor-state clustering for industrial Internet of Things fault detection
  • Article Title: Adaptive federated sensor clustering and inference framework for real time fault prioritization in industrial Internet of Things systems
  • Adaptive federated sensor clustering and inference framework for real time fault prioritization in industrial Internet of Things systems. Discover Internet of Things, 6(1), Article 270. https://doi.org/10.1007/s43926-026-00540-2

본문

A decentralized learning architecture that unites semiconductor sensor modeling with dynamic entropy-based clustering has achieved a 92.6 percent fault-detection accuracy while reducing communication traffic by 37 percent across industrial Internet of Things environments. Developed by researchers Chandrasekar Venkatachalam and Shanmugavalli Venkatachalam, the Adaptive Federated Sensor Clustering and Inference Model, abbreviated as AF-SCIM, addresses critical operational safety requirements in high-hazard industrial settings. Conventional monitoring systems in manufacturing facilities rely predominantly on centralized cloud architectures, which routinely struggle with severe communication latency, bandwidth congestion, and acute data privacy vulnerabilities when ingesting continuous telemetry from thousands of deployed instruments. Although standard federated learning provides a decentralized alternative by keeping raw training records localized on remote nodes, existing algorithmic frameworks treat incoming readings as abstract numerical arrays without accounting for physical sensor behavior. Modern factories depend heavily on solid-state semiconductor sensors because their lack of moving mechanical parts reduces physical wear, suppresses baseline noise, and provides consistent measurements across extreme operating temperatures. Nevertheless, unresolved environmental disturbances, baseline signal drift, and sudden operational mode shifts continue to degrade classical federated models, creating an urgent operational need for sensor-aware edge intelligence.

item.title: Double Deep Q-Network Cuts Simulated Railway Dispatching Errors to 0.10 Percent - Bioengineer.org
item.description:
요약

  • Subject of Research: Deep reinforcement learning and multi-source Internet of Things data fusion for dynamic railway dispatching
  • Article Title: Intelligent optimization and resource allocation system for railway dispatching empowered by the Internet of Things
  • Intelligent optimization and resource allocation system for railway dispatching empowered by the Internet of Things. Discover Internet of Things, 6(1), Article 271. https://doi.org/10.1007/s43926-026-00518-0

본문

A research team led by Pengyu Wang, Yanjun Huang, and Wanqing Guo has developed an intelligent railway dispatching and resource allocation framework that couples multi-source Internet of Things sensor data with a double deep Q-network reinforcement learning architecture. Published in Discover Internet of Things, the investigation demonstrates that integrating entropy weight and coefficient of variation adaptive weighting with deep reinforcement learning allows dynamic scheduling decisions to achieve a global maximum solution error of just 0.10 percent across complex delay conditions. Evaluated through numerical experiments on simulated mixed passenger and freight corridors, the proposed framework completed individual scheduling calculations in less than 450 milliseconds, comfortably within the one-second limit required for real-time emergency dispatching. Compared to traditional rule-based scheduling methods that exhibited a 3.40 percent error rate, the system delivered an approximately 3.3-fold improvement in solution accuracy while maintaining total weighted delay within 1000 seconds after convergence, establishing a systematic method for automated, multi-station railway traffic management.

Modern railway operations function as vital arterial lifelines for passenger transit and bulk freight distribution, yet traditional dispatching practices remain heavily constrained by centralized manual intervention, sluggish dynamic responsiveness, and inadequate multi-station coordination. When unforeseen disturbances such as unexpected train delays or section blockages occur, conventional systems struggle to ingest and synthesize rapidly evolving operating conditions across extended rail networks. Existing computational methodologies in the literature generally fall into exact mathematical formulations, metaheuristic algorithms, and baseline reinforcement learning models, each bearing distinct operational trade-offs. Exact approaches, including integer programming and Lagrangian relaxation, guarantee theoretical global optimality but suffer from exponential computational complexity as rail networks expand, rendering them incapable of achieving millisecond-level responsiveness. Metaheuristic search procedures, such as classic genetic algorithms and particle swarm optimization, accelerate convergence but frequently trap solutions within local optima during persistent delay disturbances. Meanwhile, vanilla deep Q-networks suffer from action-value overestimation bias caused by single-network architectures and lack dedicated data preprocessing pipelines.

item.title: The Path to Trillions Runs Through Networks - RFID Journal
item.description:
요약

  • Yet despite shipping billions of RFID tags and wireless trackers, the world is still operating in the dark 99.9% of the time. Most things that are made aren’t connected to the cloud in any way that is autonomous. Scans are snapshots, not connections.
  • So why is IoT the awkward stepchild of AI, when what we are really working on is a version of physical AI that could transform the economy?
  • We have all learned that the physical world is hard. I’d argue the reason is more specific than that: reading is still largely manual, and the readers that were supposed to be everywhere are not.

본문

Our industry has been working on something massively consequential for decades. Linking the physical world of places and things to the internet was always a huge idea. Add the power of AI applied to those things and the idea, and the opportunity, gets bigger still, especially if you believe that the full value of connecting physical things to the cloud has yet to be realized.

Yet despite shipping billions of RFID tags and wireless trackers, the world is still operating in the dark 99.9% of the time. Most things that are made aren’t connected to the cloud in any way that is autonomous. Scans are snapshots, not connections.

We will know we are succeeding when the links between digital and physical are counted in trillions, not billions, and, more importantly, when the cost of goods and the environmental impact of our supply chains are slashed. At that point we get to move beyond the basics of Maslow’s hierarchy to the joyful stuff: AI that goes beyond writing emails to giving us better tasting fruit, more effective medicines, and the kind of storytelling for everyday things that today we only get at a farmers’ market, a Louis Vuitton store or a top restaurant. Can we agree we are not there yet?

So why is IoT the awkward stepchild of AI, when what we are really working on is a version of physical AI that could transform the economy?

Billions, Finally

Let’s give credit where it’s due. The low-cost Bluetooth tag segment is at last experiencing the accelerated growth that has been a long time coming. Based on planned deployments from the likes of Walmart, Amazon, IFCO, the US Postal Service and McDonald’s, Bluetooth will cross the billion-tag boundary by the end of next year. Not bad for a technology originally designed to replace the wires between keyboards and PCs. Optimists like me expect annual production to eclipse the RFID industry’s 35 to 70 billion units a year before too long.

But before we pat ourselves on the back, this is a long way short of the addressable market that ABI Research and the Bluetooth SIG put at over a trillion units. The gap between a billion and a trillion is not a matter of cheaper tags. We have spent decades driving down cost, and it hasn’t happened yet. Something else is missing.

What Ambient Actually Means

“Ambient” in ambient IoT usually gets associated with harvesting energy from the light and radio waves around us. That matters, but the quality that makes ambient IoT transformative is ubiquity, and ubiquity is a function of three costs: tags, infrastructure and labor.

item.title: AI tears through legacy TCP/IP stacks, exposing vulnerabilities across critical infrastructure, OT and IoT devices - Industrial Cyber
item.description:
요약

  • AI tears through legacy TCP/IP stacks, exposing vulnerabilities across critical infrastructure, OT and IoT devices
  • Also, input validation flaws made up 16% of the findings, covering missing checks, bounds and null-termination problems. Control flow and logic bugs accounted for the smallest share at 8%, including infinite loops, null dereferences, PRNG issues and recursion.
  • By affected component, core IP, TCP, UDP, ICMP and Ethernet accounted for the largest share of newly identified vulnerabilities at 29%, followed by other components at 25% and HTTP and web servers at 15%.

본문

AI tears through legacy TCP/IP stacks, exposing vulnerabilities across critical infrastructure, OT and IoT devices

Forescout Research’s Vedere Labs found that artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted vulnerability analysis reduced the time needed to examine foundational networking software from approximately nine months to 90 hours, uncovering 99 vulnerabilities across 10 widely used TCP/IP stacks. Titled ‘Finding Critical Infrastructure Bugs with Off-the-Shelf AI,’ the research, which tested generally available AI models against open-source software and proprietary binaries, identified 66 previously unknown vulnerabilities, of which 52% were rated high or critical severity. The automated static analysis cost approximately $935, averaging $2.58 per finding, while the AI-assisted system also rediscovered 40% of previously known vulnerabilities, demonstrating ability to identify flaws in software that had already undergone extensive manual research.

The findings highlight how AI is lowering the time and cost barriers to vulnerability discovery for both security researchers and potential attackers, with implications for operational technology (OT), Internet of Things (IoT), medical devices and critical infrastructure environments. TCP/IP stacks are embedded in connected products across these sectors, meaning vulnerabilities in shared software components can affect hundreds of downstream products from multiple vendors.

Forescout noted that legacy and unsupported devices present particular challenges because they may remain operational for decades and can be difficult or impossible to patch. The company urged organizations to prioritize vulnerabilities based on reachability, exploitability and operational impact, reduce unnecessary device exposure, isolate systems that cannot be patched, accelerate patching where fixes are available, and strengthen security requirements in procurement.

“AI did not eliminate the need for expert vulnerability researchers, but it dramatically compressed the work,” Daniel dos Santos, vice president for research at Forescout, said in a Thursday media statement. “With access to an effective AI-assisted workflow, vulnerabilities in complex embedded software can be found much faster and at a fraction of the cost, by security researchers and attackers alike. Our research demonstrates that AI is changing the economics of vulnerability discovery and accelerating the pace at which security teams need to identify, prioritize, and mitigate cyber risk. This is especially impactful for critical infrastructure, where legacy and difficult-to-patch devices may remain in service for years.”

TCP/IP stacks are embedded in products used across OT, IoT, medical devices, network equipment and other cyber-physical systems. Because the same underlying software can be used across products from multiple manufacturers, a single vulnerability can create risk across the broader technology supply chain.

item.title: STMicroelectronics Adds SoftSIM and SGP.32 Support to ST87M01 NB-IoT Modules - The Fast Mode
item.description:
요약

  • STMicroelectronics has announced new capability options for users of ST87M01 NB-IoT industrial modules, with Onomondo SoftSIM, support for in-factory SGP.32-compliant SIM profile provisioning, and Zephyr ecosystem compatibility.
  • The Onomondo SoftSIM is a software-based solution running on the ST87M01 processing subsystem which makes unnecessary the use of a physical SIM device.
  • Visitors to Enlit Europe can see the ST87M01 SIM-provisioning demonstration at STMicroelectronics’ booth, B.b110, VIECON, the Vienna Congress & Convention Center, November 10-12.

본문

STMicroelectronics has announced new capability options for users of ST87M01 NB-IoT industrial modules, with Onomondo SoftSIM, support for in-factory SGP.32-compliant SIM profile provisioning, and Zephyr ecosystem compatibility.

The Onomondo SoftSIM is a software-based solution running on the ST87M01 processing subsystem which makes unnecessary the use of a physical SIM device.

This dramatically accelerates IoT-device deployment and significantly lowers production costs, reduces power consumption to relieve battery demand, and simplifies device-lifecycle and supply chain management.

At Enlit, ST will also showcase how the ST87M01 module lets equipment manufacturers perform in-factory SIM profile provisioning leveraging the SGP.32 standard, which saves stocking SIMs preconfigured for different operators. Downloading and provisioning mobile network operators’ profiles directly on the production line helps simplify inventory management while providing a consistent approach to both in-factory provisioning and remote profile management in the field, using the same SGP.32 framework.

The ST87M01 driver for Zephyr is now available through the Zephyr GitHub. It supports connectivity features including UDP, TCP, HTTP, MQTT, and CoAP, as well as GNSS, Wi-Fi positioning, and RSSI display. For developers working with Zephyr-based systems, this support can help streamline integration of the ST87M01 to take advantage of its connectivity and positioning capabilities.

The ST87M01 NB-IoT module family contains multiple variants, compliant with SGP.32 for secure remote SIM provisioning and presenting flexible options including GSMA-certified embedded SIM, GNSS/A-GNSS, Wireless M-Bus, and Wi-Fi positioning. Meeting LTE Cat NB2 Release 15, and with worldwide regional band coverage, the modules are certified in accordance with GCF, EU RED, RED-DA, FCC/ISED, PTCRB, Anatel, and Icasa. Versatile protocol support and ultra-low-power consumption allow extended maintenance-free operation, and the 12.8mm x 10.6mm LGA package is ideal for space-constrained IoT applications.

Visitors to Enlit Europe can see the ST87M01 SIM-provisioning demonstration at STMicroelectronics’ booth, B.b110, VIECON, the Vienna Congress & Convention Center, November 10-12.

ST will also present the ST87M01 and a selection of IoT solutions at electronica 2026, Messe Műnchen, Munich, November 10-13, Hall C3/booth 101.

Massimiliano Brambilla, Multisegment ASIC and Application Specific Division (MSA) Division General Manager, STMicroelectronics:

The latest software-based connectivity and SIM-management options for ST87M01 further extend the flexibility of this family for innovators to tackle the next generation of IoT applications. We have also integrated the ST87M01 with the widely adopted Zephyr framework, which makes this module series accessible within a broad open-source embedded ecosystem for all developers.

item.title: Graph-Based Framework Detects IoT Anomalies Without Labels - Bioengineer.org
item.description:
요약

  • Subject of Research: Self-supervised graph neural network for multivariate industrial IoT anomaly detection
  • Article Title: GraphContrast IoT for self supervised graph based anomaly detection in multivariate industrial IoT sensor networks
  • GraphContrast IoT for self supervised graph based anomaly detection in multivariate industrial IoT sensor networks. Discover Computing, 29(1), Article 864. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10791-026-10794-7

본문

Researchers have developed a self-supervised graph neural network framework called GraphContrast-IoT to detect anomalies in multivariate industrial Internet of Things sensor networks. Published in Discover Computing, the study addresses the limitations of current autoencoder-based and transformer-based models, which often focus primarily on temporal patterns and fail to sufficiently model the complex interactions between different sensors. By integrating physical topology with statistical correlation information, the proposed framework aims to reduce false alarms and improve detection reliability in industrial and cyber-physical systems where labelled anomaly data is scarce.

The core of the methodology involves constructing a hybrid graph that combines predefined physical connectivity with statistical inter-sensor dependencies. This hybrid adjacency matrix is estimated exclusively from normal training data and remains fixed during both training and inference. This static design eliminates the computational overhead of dynamic graph recomputation and ensures stable message passing, although it assumes that prevailing sensor relationships remain fairly constant over time. The framework does not dynamically update inter-sensor connectivity but captures changes in sensor observations within this fixed structural topology.

To learn robust representations without relying on anomaly labels, the framework employs multi-view contrastive learning. Each input time-series window is transformed into two semantically similar but stochastically perturbed views. These perturbations simulate realistic industrial disturbances, including sensor dropout to mimic communication loss, temporal warping to account for irregular sampling, and Gaussian noise injection to represent measurement errors. Additionally, controlled graph-level augmentation temporarily removes existing edges during training to enhance the model’s robustness to structural variations, while the original fixed adjacency matrix is retained for validation and inference.

The spatio-temporal encoding is handled by a specialized architecture named GCT-ADNet, which fuses graph convolution with a Temporal Convolutional Network. The graph convolution layers model spatial dependencies between physically or statistically connected sensors, while the TCN captures short- and long-term temporal dependencies within individual sensor streams. The resulting features are fused and projected into a compact latent embedding space. Anomaly scoring is then performed by calculating the Euclidean distance between each test window’s embedding and a normal reference centroid, avoiding the indirect measures of abnormality associated with reconstruction error.
